The different elements of the story are tightly interwoven to create a unified and emotionally satisfying whole. The narrative follows a clear, logical progression: it begins with the mystery of Daniel's recurring dream about an unused, sunlit flat and a heavy ring of keys, moves into the exploration of his past marriage and emotional compartmentalization through conversations with his partner Isabel, and resolves when he discovers a literal set of keys from his youth. 

Every motif introduced early on—the keys, the river running the wrong way, the thin gold light, the "spare room," and even Isabel's comment that "you never notice the last [dream]"—directly connects to and pays off in the conclusion. By taking Isabel canoeing and reclaiming the parts of himself he had packed away during his first marriage, the imagery of the dream is brought into reality (the gold light now "falling on something"), allowing the dream to naturally resolve and fade away.
